pairs.left: An ascent to God beginning in creation's traces and culminating at the crucified Christ
pairs.right: Franciscan (Bonaventure)

pairs.left: Trusting confidence expressed through small, ordinary daily acts of love
pairs.right: Carmelite (Therese of Lisieux's Little Way)

questions.explanation: Per CCC 2684, these are legitimate, complementary schools of Christian spirituality, not competing claims about the one correct way to pray -- more than one of these approaches can genuinely fit the same person's actual prayer life at once.
questions.hint: Two of these four practices come from the same broader tradition, developed a few centuries apart.

citations.quote: The personal charism of some witnesses to God's love for men has been handed on... In their rich diversity they are refractions of the one pure light of the Holy Spirit.

questions.prompt: Ignatian discernment distinguishes consolation from desolation. What is the standard counsel about decisions made in desolation?
choices: Do not change a resolution made in consolation while in desolation; hold the earlier course until clarity returns
Act quickly on whatever desolation suggests
Treat desolation as proof the earlier decision was wrong
Suspend all prayer until desolation lifts
questions.correctAnswer: Do not change a resolution made in consolation while in desolation; hold the earlier course until clarity returns
questions.explanation: The rule protects against a predictable failure: desolation makes abandonment look like realism. Ignatius counsels holding to what was decided in light rather than revising it in darkness, and if anything increasing prayer rather than reducing it.
questions.hint: The counsel concerns which state you should be in when you decide.

questions.prompt: True or False: Thérèse of Lisieux's 'Little Way' proposes an easier path than the Carmelite mysticism of Teresa of Ávila and John of the Cross.
questions.explanation: False. It is not a reduction of the demand but a relocation of it: since she could not perform great deeds, she would do small ones with complete love, and would let herself be carried rather than climb. Confidence in mercy replaces achievement — which is harder for most people than heroic effort, not easier.
questions.hint: Ask whether accepting that you cannot climb is a lower standard or a different one.

questions.prompt: What did John of the Cross mean by saying the dark night is God's work rather than the soul's failure?
choices: It is a purification God brings about, withdrawing sensible consolation so attachment shifts from the gifts to the Giver
It is punishment for unconfessed sin
It is a psychological condition to be treated
It means the person has stopped praying properly
questions.correctAnswer: It is a purification God brings about, withdrawing sensible consolation so attachment shifts from the gifts to the Giver
questions.explanation: This reverses the natural reading. The one experiencing it concludes they have failed or been abandoned; John says the darkness is the action of God on a soul that has been attached to consolations rather than to him. The distinction from ordinary dryness or from depression is exactly what a director is for.
questions.hint: Ask who is doing something in the night, on his account.

questions.prompt: Match each school of spirituality to its characteristic emphasis.

pairs.right: Interior ascent, purification, and infused contemplation
Imaginative engagement with Scripture and discernment of spirits
Lectio divina within a rhythm of ordered common prayer and work
Poverty, creation, and the humanity of Christ as the way in

questions.explanation: These are complementary routes rather than rival systems, and the tradition assumes people differ in which one fits. Insisting everyone pray in one manner is a good way to convince someone with a different temperament that they cannot pray at all.
questions.hint: One is imaginative, one ascetical and interior, one liturgical and rhythmic, one incarnational.

questions.prompt: In Ignatian discernment, what distinguishes true spiritual consolation from mere good feeling?
choices: Consolation draws the person toward God, faith, hope and love, and leaves peace; a good feeling that draws toward self-absorption or away from God is not consolation whatever it feels like
Consolation is always more intense than ordinary happiness
Any pleasant feeling during prayer is consolation
Consolation can only occur during formal prayer
questions.correctAnswer: Consolation draws the person toward God, faith, hope and love, and leaves peace; a good feeling that draws toward self-absorption or away from God is not consolation whatever it feels like
questions.explanation: The test is direction, not intensity. This matters because the enemy can offer something that feels excellent while drawing a person away — which is why discernment attends to where a movement leads rather than to how strong it is.
questions.hint: Ask what the movement is pulling you toward, not how good it feels.

questions.prompt: Ignatius describes desolation as darkness, turmoil, and being drawn toward the low and earthly. What are the three classic reasons he gives for God permitting it?
choices: Our own negligence; testing to see how we act without consolation; and to teach that consolation is a gift, not something we produce
Punishment, abandonment, and the withdrawal of grace
Illness, fatigue, and external circumstance alone
It is never permitted by God
questions.correctAnswer: Our own negligence; testing to see how we act without consolation; and to teach that consolation is a gift, not something we produce
questions.explanation: Only the first of the three is the person's fault, which already corrects the usual assumption. The third is the one that reframes everything: someone who has never lost consolation may quietly believe they generated it. Losing it teaches otherwise, and that lesson cannot be taught while it is present.
questions.hint: One reason is the person's doing; two are God's teaching.

questions.prompt: True or False: The Church teaches that trial and temptation are the same thing, since both involve difficulty.
questions.explanation: False, and the Catechism says the Holy Spirit makes us discern between the two. A trial is necessary for the growth of the inner man and leads to life; temptation leads toward sin and death. They can feel identical from inside, which is precisely why discernment is needed rather than mere endurance.
questions.hint: They differ not in how hard they are but in where they lead.

questions.prompt: Match each counsel for a time of desolation to its reason.

pairs.right: Desolation makes abandonment look like realism

pairs.left: Increase prayer rather than reduce it
pairs.right: The impulse to withdraw is the thing to resist
Secrecy is where discouragement grows strongest
Desolation presents itself as permanent, and is not

questions.explanation: Every one of these runs against what desolation itself suggests, which is the point. The counsels are not techniques for feeling better; they are a way of not making decisions in the dark that you would not make in the light.
questions.hint: Notice that each counsel is the opposite of what the state inclines you to do.

questions.prompt: Guigo II's Scala Claustralium ('The Ladder of Monks') names four movements of lectio divina in order: lectio, meditatio, oratio, and contemplatio. What is the correct order and basic content of these four movements?
choices: Reading the text attentively, reflecting on its meaning, responding to God in prayer, and resting in God's presence
Reading, then immediately resting in silence, with no reflection or verbal response involved
Praying first, then reading the text afterward as a form of thanksgiving
The four movements have no fixed order and can be done in any sequence
questions.correctAnswer: Reading the text attentively, reflecting on its meaning, responding to God in prayer, and resting in God's presence
questions.explanation: Guigo II's Scala Claustralium describes lectio (attentive reading), meditatio (reflecting on the text's meaning), oratio (responding to God in prayer), and contemplatio (resting in God's presence) as four connected movements, each doing distinct work and building on the one before it, like rungs of a single ladder.
questions.hint: Each movement's Latin name is close to its English cognate -- reading, meditating, praying, contemplating, in that order.

citations.quote: Meditation is above all a quest. The mind seeks to understand the why and how of the Christian life, in order to adhere and respond to what the Lord is asking.

questions.prompt: A person describes their prayer this way: 'The words feel empty, but I choose to stay present out of love rather than leave.' Which traditional description from the Church's spiritual writers best names what this describes?
choices: A description consistent with spiritual dryness endured in fidelity and love, which spiritual writers describe as itself a real form of prayer, not a failure of prayer
Proof that this person should stop attempting to pray altogether
A guaranteed sign that infused contemplation has now been achieved through effort
Evidence that this person has committed a mortal sin
questions.correctAnswer: A description consistent with spiritual dryness endured in fidelity and love, which spiritual writers describe as itself a real form of prayer, not a failure of prayer
questions.explanation: This description matches the traditional account of dryness endured faithfully -- itself recognized by spiritual writers as real prayer, since the choice to remain in love despite the absence of felt consolation is precisely what makes it prayer rather than technique. This app can name and recognize such an experience; it is not teaching a method for producing any further, deeper state, which -- as this topic's earlier level on infused gifts makes clear -- is not something effort can achieve.
questions.hint: The key word here is 'choose' -- an act of the will in love, not a technique for producing a feeling.

citations.quote: Dryness belongs to contemplative prayer when the heart is separated from God, with no taste for thoughts, memories, and feelings, even spiritual ones.

questions.prompt: A described meditation consists entirely of analyzing a Gospel passage's historical background and grammar, with no personal response to God at any point. What is this meditation missing, in the traditional vocabulary this level has covered?
choices: A movement from discursive analysis toward oratio -- an actual personal response of the heart to God, not just intellectual analysis of the text
Nothing -- historical and grammatical analysis alone is already the complete traditional structure of meditation
A requirement that all meditation be done in complete silence with no thought at all
A formal liturgical setting, without which meditation cannot occur
questions.correctAnswer: A movement from discursive analysis toward oratio -- an actual personal response of the heart to God, not just intellectual analysis of the text
questions.explanation: Discursive analysis of a text's meaning is real and valuable (the meditatio movement), but the traditional structure this level has covered moves from there into oratio -- an actual personal response of prayer to God arising from that reflection. Analysis alone, without ever turning to address God personally, stops short of that next movement.
questions.hint: Look back to Guigo II's four movements -- this meditation only completes the second of four steps.

citations.quote: Meditation engages thought, imagination, emotion, and desire. This mobilization of faculties is necessary in order to deepen our convictions of faith.

questions.prompt: True or False: Teresa of Ávila's seven-mansions schema and the traditional progression of stages of mental prayer (vocal prayer, meditation, affective prayer, the prayer of simplicity, infused contemplation) are two competing, contradictory maps of the spiritual life, and a person must choose only one framework to follow.
questions.explanation: These are best understood as two compatible maps describing the same underlying territory of growth in prayer, developed by different spiritual writers using different organizing images -- one a castle's mansions, the other a sequence of prayer forms -- rather than rival systems in competition with each other.
questions.hint: This is the same 'compatible maps, not competing claims' pattern this whole topic has used for its licensed diversity.

citations.quote: Christian Tradition has retained three major expressions of prayer: vocal, meditative, and contemplative.

questions.prompt: Someone experiencing spiritual dryness asks what they should actually do about it this week. Drawing on CCC 2731 and John of the Cross's guidance, which is the most accurate, sayable response?
choices: Keep showing up to pray in faithful love despite the absence of felt consolation, since perseverance through dryness -- not manufacturing a feeling -- is itself the traditional counsel
Stop praying entirely until the felt consolation naturally returns on its own
Switch permanently to a completely different religion or spiritual practice
Conclude that dryness means one should seek an intense emotional experience through any means necessary
questions.correctAnswer: Keep showing up to pray in faithful love despite the absence of felt consolation, since perseverance through dryness -- not manufacturing a feeling -- is itself the traditional counsel
questions.explanation: CCC 2731 and John of the Cross's writings on the dark night consistently counsel perseverance in faithful prayer through dryness, not seeking a technique to force consolation's return -- the fidelity itself, not a produced feeling, is what the tradition names as the real substance of prayer in this experience.
questions.hint: The traditional counsel is about persevering, not about a method for making a feeling come back.

citations.quote: Dryness belongs to contemplative prayer when the heart is separated from God... This is the moment of sheer faith clinging faithfully to Jesus in his agony and in his tomb.

questions.prompt: Given Psalm 23 ('The Lord is my shepherd'), match each lectio divina movement to what it would actually do with this text.

pairs.right: Reading the psalm slowly and attentively, noticing its actual words and images
Reflecting on what 'the Lord is my shepherd' means for one's own life and current circumstances
Responding to God in personal prayer arising from that reflection, e.g. asking for trust in his care
Resting quietly in God's presence, without further need for words

questions.explanation: This is the same four-movement structure from earlier in this level, now applied all the way through a single concrete text -- a real, sayable and doable exercise, closing this topic on an actual practice rather than one more fact to recall.
questions.hint: Each movement does one distinct job, in the same order taught earlier in this level.

citations.quote: Meditation is above all a quest. The mind seeks to understand the why and how of the Christian life, in order to adhere and respond to what the Lord is asking.

questions.prompt: How should someone tell the difference between the dark night described by John of the Cross and clinical depression?
choices: Not alone — the tradition assumes a director, and the distinction has practical consequences, since one calls for perseverance and the other for treatment
By the duration alone
The two are the same phenomenon under different names
By whether the person still attends Mass
questions.correctAnswer: Not alone — the tradition assumes a director, and the distinction has practical consequences, since one calls for perseverance and the other for treatment
questions.explanation: This matters more than most points in this topic. Reading depression as a spiritual purification can keep someone from care they need; reading purification as pathology can medicate away something God is doing. The classic signs John gives are real but they are not self-administered, and the Church's own respect for medicine applies here.
questions.hint: Notice that both wrong readings cause harm, in opposite directions.

questions.prompt: True or False: Since infused contemplation cannot be produced by any method, a person's own effort in prayer is ultimately irrelevant.
questions.explanation: False, and this is the hinge of the whole topic. What is given cannot be earned, and disposing oneself is still real work — fidelity when nothing is felt, silence kept, the heart purified. The tradition holds both without resolving the tension: God gives freely, and he ordinarily gives to those who kept showing up.
questions.hint: The tradition holds two things here that sound as though only one can be true.

questions.prompt: A person reports that after years of discursive meditation they can no longer meditate, feel drawn to simply rest in God's presence, and are troubled by having no thoughts. What does the tradition suggest?
choices: These are the classic signs of a transition from meditation toward contemplative prayer, which should be received rather than resisted by forcing discursive method
They should redouble their efforts at discursive meditation
They have lost the ability to pray and should begin again as a beginner
They are certainly experiencing the dark night of the spirit
questions.correctAnswer: These are the classic signs of a transition from meditation toward contemplative prayer, which should be received rather than resisted by forcing discursive method
questions.explanation: The inability to meditate combined with a drawing toward simple loving attention is the described pattern. The right response is not to force the earlier method back — but note the last option overreaches: naming this the dark night of the spirit is a stronger claim than the signs support, which is where a director matters.
questions.hint: Two options here are wrong by resisting the change, and one by over-diagnosing it.

questions.prompt: Match each state to what it actually is.

pairs.right: A normal season of prayer; persevere without changing course
Sloth arising from lax vigilance; met by renewed discipline
God's purifying withdrawal of consolation; discerned with a director
An illness calling for treatment, not only spiritual counsel

questions.explanation: These are frequently confused with one another, and each confusion has a cost. The last row is the one this app most wants right: a person told to pray harder through an illness has been failed, and the Church's own regard for medicine gives no ground for that advice.
questions.hint: Only one of these four is answered by anything other than prayer.
